text:
chen: Heads-up: after last night's CNI rollout to us-west2 (canary -> prod), we're seeing elevated east-west latency and intermittent pod-to-pod packet loss on GPU node pools. 

mike: saw alerts from net-ops dashboard ~02:10 UTC, latency p50 jumped from 1.8ms to ~12ms for pod pairs on same node pool. :grimacing:

ops-bot: net-alert: us-west2-gpu-pool - packet-loss spike (3m avg) = 4.2% - top talkers: training-job-* 

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T01:12Z cni-plugin=cilium@1.25.3 -> rollout complete us-west2

sara: can you paste the `kubectl get pods -o wide` for the affected node? curious if it's only RDMA-enabled instances.

chen: pasted - output below from one affected node (trimmed):
```
NAME                                 READY STATUS   RESTARTS   AGE   IP            NODE
trainer-4dfs8                        1/1   Running     0         2h    10.42.7.18    gpu-usw2-3a
model-serve-rc9                       1/1   Running     0         4h    10.42.7.44    gpu-usw2-3a
```

ip -s link show eth0 on gpu-usw2-3a:
5: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  overrun  mcast
         123456789  98765   0       1200     0        5
    TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  carrier  collisions
         98765432   87654   0       1100     0        0
```

mike: RX/TX drops around ~1k look like fragment/dropped reassembly. MTU still 1500 on host. Any changes to GSO/GRO or tunnel mode during rollout?

chen: Cilium daemonset config used `veth`+`geneve` mode for these clusters. We recently flipped `enable-gso=true` in kernel opts as part of kernel tuning image.

ryan-oncall: running `iperf3 -c` between two pod IPs shows packet loss ~3-5% and throughput oscillation. RDMA ping (`ibv_rc_pingpong`) between hosts is clean. so likely overlay/tunnel path or host offload interaction.

ops-bot: note: a subset of nodes (gpu-usw2-3a/3b) have custom kernel image (gso tuning) applied last week.

mike: quick mitigation: try disabling GSO/GRO on affected nodes to see if drops stop. command:`sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off`

chen: just ran that on gpu-usw2-3a - immediate improvement in packet loss for pods on that node (drop -> 0.2%), p50 latency down to 2.5ms. But CPU overhead increased for pod networking (seen +6% on node).

sara: good test. suggests offload+geneve interaction. We should confirm by switching CNI tunnel to `vxlan` on a single node and retesting before cluster-wide rollback.

mike: created canary daemonset patch to force `tunnel=vxlan` on one node (gpu-usw2-3b) and enabling `tunnel=geneve` on rest for comparison. will run perf tests in 10m.

chen: also saw `dmesg` logs with `skb_frag_list error` and kernel warnings about `gso fragment` around the same time as rollout. copying snippet:
```
[Mar 17 01:14:22] skb_frag: gso error: fraglist corrupt?
[Mar 17 01:14:22] geneve: RX drop on softnet: skb GSO failed
```

ryan-oncall: raising severity with infra-owners and Cilium upstream. filing issue referencing kernel/gso interaction + our geneve config + RDMA node specifics.

deploy-bot: rollback option available: cilium@1.25.2 -> can target only us-west2 via rollout flag. use `--region us-west2` to restrict.

sara: proposed plan: 1) Finish vxlan canary + perf tests 2) If vxlan stable, patch config to force vxlan across gpu pools and monitor 3) schedule controlled rollback to 1.25.2 if problem persists 4) long term: coordinate with kernel team on GSO/GRO tuning or upstream fix.

mike: timeline: run canary tests 10:30 UTC, collect `pktstat`, `tc -s qdisc`, `kubectl top node`, `sar -n DEV 1 20`. will attach results.

chen: thanks. adding `@sre` and `@kernel-team` to the follow-up ticket. putting emergency label on this ticket.

ops-bot: incident-tracker: INC-2026-042 created for us-west2-gpu-cni-packet-loss by chen

ryan-oncall: if we need quick capacity recovery for customer training jobs, we can evacuate affected pods to eu-west1/gpu pool until fix is in. but note cost & data gravity.

sara: acknowledged. let's avoid full rollback until we confirm vxlan fix; rollback has bigger blast radius.

chen: I'll post test artifacts and `tcpdump` captures to the incident ticket. will update once canary completes. :eyes:
